title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier-Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared-Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We report a preregistered, autonomous, paired emulation study (study-cnd-2026-001) that evaluated whether a verifier-assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline improves operational correctness of LLM-produced network configurations on vendor-diverse emulated NetOps tasks. Critically, the frozen execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics: each pair reused the same initial generated candidate (both conditions), so the guarded pipeline's repair stage could only trigger if that single candidate failed validation. Under this exact design (Npairs=200; planned_episode_count=400; model=gpt-5-mini; validator=deterministic_netops_validator_v5; repair budget ≤1 call/task), both baseline and guarded conditions produced oracle-passing configurations for all 200 paired tasks (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar two-sided p = 1.00). We release the full artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, model-call traces, validator traces, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts) and interpret the null confirmatory result in light of the preregistered shared-generation semantics, task construction, and validator scope. We conclude with reproducibility-minded recommendations for future guarded-pipeline evaluations.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate natural-language intent into device configuration artifacts for NetOps. Prior work documents LLM failure modes (hallucination, unsafe ordering, vendor-idiom errors) and advocates verifier-anchored workflows (generate→validate→repair) to improve operational reliability [see Related Work]. We preregistered and executed an autonomous, paired confirmatory experiment to test whether a verifier-assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rate relative to unconstrained generation on a curated emulated task bank. The preregistered primary estimand was the absolute paired success-rate difference: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and deterministic execution manifest for a paired NetOps evaluation (study-cnd-2026-001); (2) a fully archived execution and analysis bundle (prompts, validator, model-call traces, hashes); (3) a transparent, artifact-grounded report of the confirmatory null outcome under the exact frozen design and a diagnostic analysis of why the guarded path was not exercised. Research question (precise): Does the verifier-assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increase the oracle pass rate relative to unconstrained LLM generation under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate execution semantics and the other frozen design choices?
sections.related_work: Evaluations of LLMs for intent→configuration translation and guarded-agent workflows have proliferated. NetConfEval and NetBuddy study translation quality and failure modes for intent-driven configuration [Chang et al.; Wang et al.]. MeshAgent and constraint-based adaptation show reliability gains when external invariants are encoded and validated [Zhou et al.]. Verifier-grounded workflows in other domains (StruSpec for music programs) demonstrate that execution+verification plus targeted counterexamples can enable effective repairs [Ding]. Our study differs by preregistering a deterministic paired confirmatory design, freezing generation semantics (shared initial candidate), and publishing a full immutable artifact set to enable reproducible inspection of why a guarded pipeline did or did not produce a measurable improvement.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. The experiment was preregistered as study-cnd-2026-001 prior to observing outcomes. Key elements (frozen): paired binary design (conditions = baseline vs guarded), Npairs = 200, protocol buckets (BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN evenly distributed), vendor stratification (Cisco/Juniper/Arista), generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (both conditions used the same initial generated candidate per pair), model = gpt-5-mini (declared), validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (deterministic emulation-based oracle), repair budget = at most one repair call per task, analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1 (paired bootstrap + McNemar). The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration SHA-256: a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2). Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator created 200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks with explicit initial and expected-final states and workflow constraints (examples: shutdown_before_mtu_change, make-before-break). Each task includes a required-sequence and a difficulty tag (simple/complex/medium/hard). Execution semantics and adapter. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter implemented shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generated candidate produced in a shared stage and recorded; both baseline and guarded conditions consumed that same candidate). Model and calls. All calls used the declared model string gpt-5-mini via the hosted provider; configuration metadata are archived (execution/model_configuration.json, sha256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Validator/oracle. The deterministic validator executes candidate commands against a containerized device emulator and returns a structured pass/fail plus counterexamples (validator artifact: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; validator traces archived under execution/scoring/). Analysis plan. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed with paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) and an exact two-sided McNemar test on the paired contingency. Missingness policy: complete-pair primary analysis (pairs with provider/infrastructure failures would be logged and excluded); execution manifest documents zero failed episodes and no provider-drift events.
sections.results: Execution accounting. The autonomous run completed all planned episodes: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (shared-initial semantics produced one model-generation per pair). Analysis outcome (confirmatory): complete_pairs = 200; baseline_successes = 200/200 (1.00); guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.00); paired difference = 0.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (bootstrap_resamples = 10,000; seed = 1729); McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Deterministic reconciliation. The deterministic reconciliation artifact confirms marginal and pair accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; sha256: 799b23b993fcc9c04fc4d0a375e975937bc11d9f8c6595d43dce94375411d174). Why guarded did not show improvement. Because of shared_initial_candidate semantics, baseline and guarded consumed identical initial candidates for each pair; in all 200 pairs the shared initial candidate passed the deterministic oracle, so the guarded repair path was never invoked. The analysis artifacts supporting these facts include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (n_11=200, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0; sha256: 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (baseline and guarded success rates both 1.0; sha256: 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951). Representative scoring example. A canonical scored episode is archived at execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256: eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b) and its paired guarded artifact execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256: b8b05283d639081f5c1f802a7ad62ae17a98f15bba1809720e0e4f3253fd2b23). The shared generated candidate for that pair is in execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (sha256: f8de4d6e1a625e42ba4907440b4377c78949ed56446e5c73030bc267e56abfaf). All execution and scoring artifacts and the full hash manifest are in the execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/* paths recorded in the manifest).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and scope. The preregistered null confirmatory result is definitive for the exact frozen design: with shared_initial_candidate semantics, gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and the provided task bank, the guarded pipeline produced no measurable improvement because the shared initial candidates already satisfied the oracle in every pair. This outcome does not imply that verifier-assisted pipelines cannot improve correctness in other designs. Instead it highlights three design axes that control observable benefit: (1) generation independence (shared vs independent generation); (2) task difficulty and oracle coverage (synthetic tasks here were solvable by the shared candidate generator); and (3) repair budget and policy (preregistration limited repairs to ≤1 call/task; the repair stage was never triggered). Practical lessons for future studies. (i) Use independent-condition generation when estimating guardrail efficacy unless shared-generation semantics are intentionally the subject of study. (ii) Pre-evaluate oracle coverage to detect trivial-accept cases (oracle_coverage diagnostics are part of our artifact bundle). (iii) Report deterministic reconciliation and per-call hashes to allow artifact-level auditing; we publish these artifacts. Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial semantics intentionally reduces variability and can mask pipeline effects; we made this choice in the preregistration and record it transparently. Construct validity: the emulator-based oracle enforces syntactic and semantic predicates but may not capture all operational failure modes of live devices. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic task bank limit generalizability. Conclusion validity: with complete pairs = 200 and unanimous passes, statistical tests confirm a null effect under the frozen design; no multiple-comparison corrections are required for the single preregistered estimand.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study comparing unconstrained LLM generation to a verifier-assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline. Under the exact frozen design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator, task bank of 200), both conditions passed the oracle for every paired task; therefore the preregistered advantage hypothesis was not supported. The artifact-backed analysis shows that shared-generation semantics and task construction explain why the guarded repair path was never exercised. We release the full artifact bundle to enable reproduction and to support future preregistered studies that vary generation independence, oracle coverage, model families, and repair budgets. Our principal methodological recommendation is explicit preregistration of generation semantics (shared vs independent) because that choice materially affects observable pipeline benefit.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure Statement (artifact-backed): This study was produced by an autonomous research run launched from the frozen initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The experiment was preregistered as study-cnd-2026-001 (preregistration SHA-256: a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2) and executed under the frozen plan recorded in the execution manifest. LLM and adapter: all generation used the declared model identifier gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses) via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family; model call configuration is archived at execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Preregistered experimental design (frozen): paired confirmatory design with Npairs=200, protocol buckets = {BGP, OSPF, ACL, VLAN}, vendor stratification = {Cisco, Juniper, Arista}, primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, maximum repair calls per task = 1, analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1 (bootstrap resamples = 10,000; seed = 1729). Crucial execution semantics recorded in the preregistration and manifest: generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (a single generated candidate per pair produced during a shared stage and consumed by both baseline and guarded conditions). This shared-initial choice was preregistered and materially affected results: in this run every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic oracle, so the guarded repair path was not invoked for any pair (artifacts: execution/*; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256: 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c; analysis/condition_summary.csv sha256: 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951). Validator and emulator: the oracle/validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (emulation-based), and all validator traces and scores are archived under execution/scoring/ (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json sha256: eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b). Execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation: the run completed planned_episode_count=400 and completed_episode_count=400 with model_calls_used=200 and failed_episode_count=0; deterministic reconciliation artifact confirms accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json sha256: 799b23b993fcc9c04fc4d0a375e975937bc11d9f8c6595d43dce94375411d174). Autonomous scope and human role: the Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and collaborated pre-lock on infrastructure rehearsals; per the autonomy boundary, all substantive research formulation, preregistration, literature review, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting occurred autonomously after the lock. No human manual editing of substantive technical content occurred post-lock. Tooling and artifact release: prompts, task manifests, raw model outputs, provider-call traces, validator traces, analysis artifacts, and full hash manifests were recorded immutably and are available in the execution bundle paths enumerated in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/*). Deviations and failures: none recorded that affect the primary confirmatory analysis; no provider/model-identifier drift events occurred during the run. Limitations imposed by the frozen design (explicit): shared_initial_candidate semantics, single-model scope (gpt-5-mini), deterministic emulator oracle, and limited repair budget (≤1 repair call/task).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic task bank of 200); results do not generalize beyond these frozen choices.
Shared-initial-candidate execution semantics eliminated independent variation between baseline and guarded conditions and therefore prevented the guarded pipeline from exercising repairs in this run.
Synthetic emulated tasks and a deterministic emulator-based oracle do not fully represent production heterogeneity (real devices, live telemetry, transient faults, vendor-image idiosyncrasies).
Single-model experiment limits generality across LLM families, instruction-tuning regimes, and deployment-specific behaviors.
Repair budget was restricted to one repair call per preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored.
Oracle blind spots (coverage gaps) are possible; artifact flags (oracle-coverage-ambiguous) are present in the bundle where applicable.
